h1.no_claim_reason: the title claims only that APOE binds TREM2 (polarity unknown) and the mechanism says TREM2 'regulates' survival and the pair is 'tied' to AD; no direction of APOE or TREM2 on Alzheimer disease or on microglial survival is stated in the title or mechanism (only the falsification implies APOE knockout lowers microglial survival)

h2.note: sign from the mechanism: MS4A4A lowers TREM2 'thereby ... contributing to disease risk'; the chain has MS4A4A -| TREM2 but no signed step from TREM2 to Alzheimer disease, and MS4A4A-AD is unsigned

h3.no_claim_reason: the title says the three genes 'coordinate' the microglial response and plaque compaction, the mechanism that PLCG2 and ABI3 'modulate' plaque structure and that rare variants 'associate' with risk; no direction on Alzheimer disease for INPP5D, PLCG2 or ABI3 is stated (PLCG2 -| plaques is signed only in step h3.2 and the falsification)

findings.detail: h1 is a restated protein interaction (APOE binds TREM2, from one STRING edge) with no direction of either gene on Alzheimer disease, so nothing can be composed or tested.
h3 names three genes that 'coordinate' a response but gives no direction for any of them on Alzheimer disease, so no claim can be tested.
h1.1 is a binding with unknown polarity, so no sign passes from APOE to TREM2 or on to microglial survival; APOE's effect on anything is unstated.
h2 is a star, not a chain: h2.1 ends at TREM2, h2.2 starts again from MS4A4A, and no step links TREM2 to Alzheimer disease with a sign, so the claim MS4A4A ->+ AD risk has no route.
h3 is four disjoint steps (INPP5D -| RIPK1; PLCG2 -| plaques; ABI3 ~ plaques; INPP5D ~ AD) with no step joining INPP5D, PLCG2 and ABI3, although the title says they 'coordinate'.
the PLCG2 and ABI3 parts of h3 end at amyloid plaques and never reach Alzheimer disease.

PMID:42357928, the only citation for 'PLCG2 decreases amyloid plaques', says the protective P522R variant left total amyloid burden unaffected and only increased plaque compaction; the run turned compaction into a decrease in amount, and the text is about the variant, not PLCG2 level.
decreases_amount is applied to a phenotype ('amyloid plaques'); curated as an effect on the phenotype HP:0100256 Senile plaques.

TREM2 ~ AD is left unsigned (polarity unknown) although the run's own citation PMID:28714976 gives an odds ratio (R62H, OR 1.67); the step is about the gene, so the allele's sign could not be carried over.

INPP5D ~ AD is left unsigned and cited only to an Open Targets score, while the run's h3.1 citation PMID:41633359 says INPP5D deficiency promotes RIPK1-mediated neuroinflammation, neuronal loss and LOAD-relevant pathology.
ABI3 ~ plaques is left unsigned; its citation PMID:42092345 gives a direction for the S212F variant (lower dense-core plaque compaction and burden) but not for ABI3 itself.

the h3 mechanism says rare PLCG2 and ABI3 variants associate with AD risk; PMID:28714976 (cited only at h1.3) gives signed rows for both (PLCG2 rs72824905 OR 0.68 protective, ABI3 rs616338 OR 1.43 risk), but no step of the run states either association.
the mechanism says INPP5D represses pro-inflammatory mediators via RIPK1 and that PLCG2/ABI3 redistribute microglia; the chain stops at RIPK1 and at plaques.

PMID:42689388 supports TREM2 -> microglial survival but is about sAPPalpha, not APOE, as the TREM2 ligand; h1's APOE-TREM2 link rests only on a STRING edge whose score is mostly text-mining (0.99; experimental 0.58).
no hypothesis lists any supporting or contradicting evidence (all lists empty); sources.json holds only chain citations.

every chain node except Alzheimer disease (MONDO:0004975) has an empty CURIE, including the cell type 'mature microglial cell', which the run itself cites as CL_0002629 in its abstention evidence IDs.
four of nine steps (h1.3, h2.2, h3.3, h3.4) are associated_with with unknown polarity, so every gene-to-disease link in the run is unsigned and nothing can compose to Alzheimer disease.

the guide takes a claim's sign only from title or mechanism; here the falsification tests state directions the title and mechanism do not (h1: APOE knockout lowers microglial survival; h3: PLCG2 knockout raises plaques), so h1 and h3 got no claim.

the guide's no_direction row names OT scores without saying it only applies to steps that need a sign, and no evidence kind names them; an OT score states both ends of an unsigned associated_with step, so it is kept here as observational (as in the reference run 20260824T223623Z-4f7d1a), but the first pass excluded all three.
taxon has no value for non-human primate; PMID:41435829's span rests on knockout/antibody work in macrophages, microglia, NHPs and mice, recorded as mechanistic with taxon mouse.

the PMID:41633359 abstract does not say the design or species behind 'Repression of RIPK1 kinase by INPP5D' (SH2-domain binding at p-Y383 plus 'microglial INPP5D deficiency'); recorded as inVitro with no taxon.

the guide does not say whether a variant-in-gene result (knock-in, GWAS row) counts for a gene-level step; it is kept here for unsigned gene associations (h1.3, h3.3); at h3.2 the question does not arise, because the PLCG2 knock-in text states no decrease in plaques even for the variant.

'microglial survival' is GO:0043066 negative regulation of apoptotic process (exact synonym 'pro-survival') refined to CL:0002629, which leaves out non-apoptotic death; the closer GO:0060548 negative regulation of cell death is in the corpus only through ECOCORE/planarian imports, so render.py gives it no kind and rejects it.

the only 'established' statement in the run (belief 4/5) is APOE binds TREM2 from one STRING edge whose combined score is mostly text-mining (0.99; experimental 0.58), while one observational record, a three-stage exome GWAS of 85,133 subjects for TREM2 ~ AD, gives 1/2 (2/3 with the OT score added).

a background phrase ('INPP5D, an important LOAD risk gene'; 'The Alzheimer's disease risk genes MS4A4A and MS4A6A') counts as review at 3/5 on its own, more than the primary GWAS row at h1.3 on its own (1/2); with the OT scores added, h2.2 and h3.4 reach 5/7 and h1.3 only 2/3.

h2's falsification test (knock out MS4A4A in microglia, measure TREM2 protein) is the experiment its own citation PMID:41435829 already reports ('By modulating MS4A4A using knockout ... in macrophages, microglia ... MS4A4A and MS4A6A are negative regulators of both the transmembrane and soluble TREM2 proteins'), so it tests nothing new.

the title says MS4A4A regulates TREM2 'expression' and h2.1 is a direct MS4A4A -| TREM2 step, but PMID:41435829 says the effect is indirect and post-transcriptional (MS4A4A protects MS4A6A from degradation; MS4A6A blocks DAP12, which sets TREM2 levels); the net sign is right, the mediator is missing.

the abstention for RNPS1 and LPIN2 cites OT:RNPS1-MONDO_0004975, PMID:41865408, PMID:21283692 and two CXG records, none of which is in sources.json, so the abstention cannot be checked against its texts.
